coverage.rationale: Every spatial measurement depends on a stable body-diameter normalization from both recordings.
Two loadout-controlled airborne traverses bound ordinary horizontal movement despite differing player input.
Two early-match arcs with no player-movement card establish a deliberately broad jump-height band.
The same independent arcs bound time to apex at the source's two-tick frame resolution.
The SSAG opening loadout leaves projectile speed unchanged and supplies the accepted base-speed sample.
coverage.limitation: The independent WCG opening uses Thruster and Fast Forward, so its projectile sample is retained as a contaminated comparison and does not count toward coverage.

coverage.rationale: The SSAG opening provides a visible unmodified projectile-core radius.
coverage.limitation: At 640x360 the core is only about three pixels across, so a second recording would not materially improve the broad tolerance without higher-resolution media.

coverage.rationale: Pre-shot and post-shot body velocities from both opening rounds produce a low-confidence recoil impulse band.
Both opening loadouts leave block duration unchanged and expose the visible active shield.
Both recordings use a fixed 16:9 full-stage view with independently measured body scale.
One clean WCG ring-out exposes the boundary-to-result transition.
coverage.limitation: The selected SSAG opening death is projectile-driven rather than an observable ring-out, so no second out-of-bounds sample is claimed.
